items.followUp: Write any two physical properties of metals.

rubric.why: Poor conductivity of heat or electricity is a physical property of non-metals.
rubric.description: Gives poor conductivity as one physical property.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying non-metals as poor conductors.

rubric.why: Solid non-metals are generally brittle and are not malleable or ductile.
rubric.description: Gives a second physical property of non-metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct property distinct from the first.

modelAnswer: Non-metals are generally poor conductors of heat and electricity.
Solid non-metals are generally brittle, non-malleable and non-ductile.

items.followUp: State four conclusions drawn from Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment.

rubric.why: Most alpha particles passed straight through the foil without deflection.
rubric.description: States that most alpha particles passed through the foil without deflection.

rubric.why: Some alpha particles were deflected through small angles.
rubric.description: States that some alpha particles were slightly deflected.

rubric.why: Very few alpha particles were sharply deflected or turned back.
rubric.description: States that very few alpha particles were deflected through large angles or turned back.

rubric.why: The scattering results showed that the atom is mostly empty space and that its positive charge is concentrated in a small, dense nucleus.
rubric.description: Gives a conclusion drawn from the experiment.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that the atom is mostly empty space or that positive charge is concentrated in a small, dense nucleus.

modelAnswer: Most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil without any deflection.
Some alpha particles were deflected through small angles.
Very few alpha particles were deflected through large angles or turned back.
These results showed that most of the atom is empty space and that its positive charge is concentrated in a small, dense nucleus.

items.followUp: Define an unsaturated solution and describe how a supersaturated solution can be prepared.

rubric.why: A saturated solution contains the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve at a specified temperature.
rubric.description: Defines a saturated solution in terms of the maximum amount of dissolved solute at a particular temperature.

rubric.why: A supersaturated solution contains more dissolved solute than a saturated solution normally holds at the same temperature.
rubric.description: Defines a supersaturated solution by its excess dissolved solute at a particular temperature.

rubric.why: Heating a saturated solution allows additional solute to dissolve.
rubric.description: States that the saturated solution is heated and extra solute is dissolved in it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the heating and additional-solute step.

rubric.why: Slow, undisturbed cooling can leave the excess solute dissolved, producing a supersaturated solution.
rubric.description: States that the hot solution is cooled carefully to obtain a supersaturated solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the cooling step and resulting solution.

modelAnswer: A saturated solution contains the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve in a given amount of solvent at a particular temperature.
A supersaturated solution contains more dissolved solute than a saturated solution can normally hold at that temperature.
To prepare one, heat a saturated solution and dissolve some additional solute in it.
Then cool the hot solution slowly and undisturbed; the excess solute remains dissolved, forming a supersaturated solution.
